title: Vanishing of Fourier coefficients from a uniform zero-free half-plane, and an uncertainty principle for involutions in PGL₂(𝔽_ℓ)
description:
A mathematical note (preprint) and a Lean 4 formalisation. Write Z(θ) for the statement that every Dedekind zeta function is nonzero in Re s > θ, uniformly in the field; Cureton and Thorner state Z(1 − 1/6000) in a preprint, and their Lean development (AxiomMath/DedekindZetaZeroFree, commit 09afbb4c; proofs generated by AxiomProver) proves Z(31/32), a constant that is not in the preprint (v1). The note records the transfer of the Serre / Murty–Murty–Saradha / Zywina argument to this setting: for a non-CM newform f with integer coefficients, Z(θ) implies #{p ≤ x : a_f(p) = 0} ≪ x^{(1+θ)/2}, so #{p ≤ x : τ(p) = 0} ≪ x^{63/64} given the Lean theorem. This implication is verified in Lean 4 in the form x^{(1+θ)/2+ε}, conditional on an explicit hypothesis encoding the mod-ℓ Galois representations and their large image (Deligne, Ribet–Momose, Swinnerton-Dyer), which is not formalised. The main new ingredient is an exact inequality for the involutions of PGL₂(𝔽_ℓ): every nonnegative class-function majorant φ satisfies μ(φ)λ_A(φ) ≥ κ_ℓ ≥ 1 − 1/ℓ (λ_A Bellaïche's Littlewood norm); it gives lower bounds, at the exponent (1+θ)/2, for three explicitly defined error functionals (single-ℓ majorants, single-extension Chebotarev certificates over fields whose Galois group maps onto ∏ PGL₂(𝔽_ℓ) with central kernel, per-prime Selberg sieves with pairwise error accounting). The repository also contains the scripts and output logs of the finite computations cited in the note.

The note was prepared with substantial AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic, run as agents under the author's direction); the author takes responsibility for it and is verifying the proofs. It has not been refereed.
